title: Fun enough to see what you get, but certainly not worth the cost.
text: I was definitely not expecting to receive anything spectacular with this subscription box, but what I got was below expectations. I would say that 80% of it was just pure junk unless you have a very specific project to use it for. Both orders I received included video cards that were not actually all that bad, but most of the rest of it was unusable (for me anyway). My second box included an old Intel motherboard that I was able to sell on eBay for $20, which recouped some of what I paid for the box, but it arrived absolutely filthy-- it was caked with dust that I had to clean off just to get it to point where I felt comfortable selling it, not to mention the fact that I felt as if I needed to test it before selling, so that was a decent amount of work just to recoup some of the money I spent. Honestly, the Excelius branded tchotchkes they include with every box are probably the best part of the whole deal. You might get an optical drive for a laptop, but that doesn't do you a whole lot of good unless you have the same model laptop with a faulty optical drive, or if you care to take the time to sell it on eBay for $10 or less. To be clear, you are paying $30 for the fun of opening up a box to see what might be useful to you out of $20+ worth of discarded electronics. I am not unhappy that I did it for two months, but I can't help but feel like now I have to find some way to get rid of most of this crap. You'd be way better off analyzing what old components you actually need and spending that same $30 (or less) on those parts elsewhere.
label: negative
